record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: Can the graph neighbors of a query point be computed approximately rather than exactly, while guaranteeing that the resulting approximation does not adversely affect classification error?

evidence.quote: Another fertile area which has not been investigated concerns the efficient computation of the graph neighbors of a query point, approximately, rather than exactly, with the constraint that the error in classification not be adversely affected.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let $S=\{(x_1,y_1),\dots,(x_n,y_n)\}\subset X\times\{1,\dots,c\}$ be a labeled training set. Fix an integer $k\ge 1$ and define the $k$-nearest-neighbor graph $G_k(S)$ on $S$ in which each $x_i$ is connected to its $k$ nearest neighbors in $S\setminus\{x_i\}$ under $d$. For a query point $q\in X$, let $N_k(q)\subseteq S$ denote the set of exact $k$ graph neighbors of $q$ (the $k$ points of $S$ closest to $q$), and let $\hat h_k(q)$ be the classifier that assigns to $q$ the plurality label among $N_k(q)$. Let $\mathcal D$ be an unknown distribution on $X\times\{1,\dots,c\}$ from which $S$ and test points are drawn i.i.d., and let $\mathrm{err}(\hat h_k)=\Pr_{(q,y)\sim\mathcal D}[\hat h_k(q)\ne y]$ denote its classification error.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm $\mathcal A$ which, given $S$, $k$ and a query point $q$, returns a set $\widetilde N_k(q)\subseteq S$ of size $k$ (a possibly approximate set of graph neighbors) using strictly sub-linear time in $n$ per query, and induces a classifier $\tilde h_k$ via plurality vote on $\widetilde N_k(q)$, such that for every distribution $\mathcal D$ and every $n$,
$$\mathrm{err}(\tilde h_k)\le \mathrm{err}(\hat h_k)+\varepsilon(n),$$
with $\varepsilon(n)\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ (or, more strongly, $\varepsilon(n)=0$)? Characterize the conditions on $(X,d)$, on $\mathcal D$, and on the approximation rule used by $\mathcal A$ under which the approximate neighbor computation provably does not adversely affect classification error.
artifact.status_search_result: Approximate nearest-neighbor search with classification-error guarantees has been studied extensively; recent work (e.g., on instance-based approximation guarantees for graph-based ANNS) provides per-instance distance-ratio guarantees but does not fully resolve the question of when approximate neighbor retrieval preserves the Bayes/empirical classification error in all settings. The general problem as posed appears not to have a definitive, settled answer in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Instance-based Approximation Guarantees for Graph-based Nearest Neighbor Search
status_evidence.snippet: Graph-based approaches for approximate nearest neighbor search do not come with a priori approximation guarantees... method provides tight instance-based approximation guarantee.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses per-instance guarantees for graph-based ANN, indicating that worst-case classification-error guarantees remain a non-trivial concern.

status_evidence.title: Graph-based Nearest Neighbor Search: From Practice to Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical analysis of graph-based ANN search.
status_evidence.claim: Theory for graph-based ANN exists but does not directly bound induced classification error in general.
